claims.text: Low-temperature plasma nitriding of CoCrFeMnNi will produce a thin, uniform, nitride-rich surface layer.
The nitride-rich surface layer will increase surface hardness relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi.
The nitriding treatment will improve room-temperature creep resistance by increasing dislocation pinning.
The nitriding treatment will enhance corrosion resistance by establishing a stable passive film.
A solution-treated, coarse-grained CoCrFeMnNi state is typically used for aerospace fasteners.
Plasma nitriding at approximately 400°C for 6 hours in an N2-H2 atmosphere is an appropriate intervention.
The proposed processing conditions can avoid bulk microstructural degradation while modifying only the near-surface region.
The modified layer will contain a fine dispersion of nitrides.
The hardened nitride-rich layer will improve wear resistance.
The nitride-rich layer will act as a barrier against corrosive environments.
Nitrogen diffusion during plasma nitriding forms a thin nitride layer in CoCrFeMnNi.
The nitride layer impedes dislocation motion and thereby reduces room-temperature creep.
The nitride layer promotes passivation and thereby improves corrosion resistance.
Nitrided specimens will have a lower room-temperature creep rate than untreated specimens, particularly when deformation is surface-dominated.
Nitrided specimens will exhibit lower corrosion current density than untreated specimens.
The beneficial effects will generally be confined to the upper tens of micrometers of the material.
Over-nitriding can compromise the effectiveness of the modified surface layer.
Extreme cyclic loading can cause fatigue-induced delamination and compromise the nitrided layer.
Service temperatures significantly above 400°C may compromise the nitrided layer's effectiveness.
